LiFePO4 buffer pack with boost converter

ideas.rationale: Holding wall draw flat and letting a battery supply the high-power bursts cuts peak demand and the transformer's no-load losses, and lets the oven run on off-peak or solar power.

ideas.title: Solid-state GaN generator replaces magnetron and high-voltage chain

new_nodes.label: GaN solid-state RF power amplification at 2.45 GHz
new_nodes.detail: Gallium-nitride transistors amplify a low-power 2.45 GHz oscillator to 700 W from a low-voltage DC rail, with no cathode, filament or kilovolt supply.

new_nodes.label: GaN RF amplifier module
new_nodes.detail: Heater-free solid-state generator that starts instantly and can run anywhere from 0 to 100 percent power.

new_nodes.label: Universal 48 V DC switch-mode supply
new_nodes.detail: Mains-to-low-voltage supply accepting 120 V or 230 V, replacing the HV transformer, voltage doubler and capacitor.

new_nodes.label: Continuous RF power modulation
new_nodes.detail: Analog power level replaces the 5-step duty-cycle cam, so the oven never cycles on and off.

new_edges.to: GaN solid-state RF power amplification at 2.45 GHz

new_edges.from: GaN solid-state RF power amplification at 2.45 GHz

ideas.rationale: Removing the filament, high-voltage transformer and magnetron warm-up losses, and letting power track each load continuously, cuts the watts burned before any food is heated.

ideas.title: Phased-array feeds replace the turntable assembly

new_nodes.label: Four-port phased-array feed
new_nodes.detail: Four small 2.45 GHz feeds on cavity walls, each with phase and amplitude control, steer the field pattern electronically.

new_nodes.label: Electronic hot-spot sweeping
new_nodes.detail: Shifts field maxima around the cavity by changing feed phases, flattening heating with no moving parts.

new_nodes.label: Multi-feed RF phase steering in a reverberant cavity
new_nodes.detail: Relative phase between feeds shifts interference nodes so cold spots move and average out.

new_nodes.label: Fixed glass tray
new_nodes.detail: Non-rotating tray that needs no roller ring or motor.

new_edges.to: Multi-feed RF phase steering in a reverberant cavity

new_edges.from: Multi-feed RF phase steering in a reverberant cavity

ideas.rationale: Replacing the 5 rpm motor and rotating assembly with electronically swept hot spots removes a continuous mechanical draw and evens heating so food finishes in fewer minutes.

ideas.title: Doneness-sensing auto-stop replaces timer and power knobs

new_nodes.label: Metal-oxide gas sensor array
new_nodes.detail: Vent-mounted sensor reads moisture and volatile compounds to infer how cooked the food is.

new_nodes.label: Microcontroller cook controller
new_nodes.detail: Single electronic controller with one dial replaces the mechanical timer and power knob.

new_nodes.label: Mechanical clockwork timer knob (0-30 min)
new_nodes.detail: Legacy part, added so the substitution is explicit.

new_nodes.label: 5-step duty-cycle power knob
new_nodes.detail: Legacy part, added so the substitution is explicit.

new_nodes.label: Doneness-based RF cutoff
new_nodes.detail: Stops RF emission when the sensed state reaches the target rather than after a fixed time.

new_nodes.label: Metal-oxide gas sensing with cook-curve algorithms
new_nodes.detail: Tracks humidity and volatile-compound rise and classifies the food's state.

new_edges.to: Metal-oxide gas sensing with cook-curve algorithms

new_edges.from: Metal-oxide gas sensing with cook-curve algorithms

ideas.rationale: Ending RF emission at sensed doneness instead of a fixed timer stops the magnetron before food is overcooked or reheated, so no energy is spent beyond what the food needs.

ideas.title: Load-matched telescoping cavity

new_nodes.label: Telescoping cavity back wall
new_nodes.detail: Motorised RF-tight metal shutter that sets cavity depth to the food size and keeps the field resonant.

new_nodes.label: Load-matched RF absorption
new_nodes.detail: Keeps the field concentrated on small loads so less energy reflects back or heats empty space.

new_nodes.label: Variable-depth resonant cavity via movable short-circuit plane
new_nodes.detail: A sliding conductive plane changes the resonant length of the cavity without changing its footprint.

new_edges.to: Variable-depth resonant cavity via movable short-circuit plane

new_edges.from: Variable-depth resonant cavity via movable short-circuit plane

ideas.rationale: Resizing the cavity to the food keeps the magnetron working into a well-matched load so small portions heat without pumping full power into an empty 20 L box.

ideas.title: Thermoelectric harvest of magnetron waste heat

new_nodes.label: Thermoelectric generator (Bi2Te3) on magnetron wrapper
new_nodes.detail: Converts part of the magnetron's waste heat to DC to run low-power loads such as the turntable motor.

new_nodes.label: Waste-heat electricity harvesting
new_nodes.detail: Offsets the mains draw of the turntable motor and control electronics.

new_nodes.label: Seebeck thermoelectric conversion
new_nodes.detail: Bismuth telluride couples turn a temperature difference into voltage with no moving parts.

ideas.rationale: Converting part of the magnetron's otherwise wasted heat into electricity offsets mains draw for the turntable motor and controls, so less grid energy is consumed per cook.

new_nodes.detail: A low-cost coupler tap and RF diode on the existing waveguide duct, read by the controller ADC, replaces the mechanical cam timer.

new_nodes.label: Reflected-power load sensing
new_nodes.detail: Reflected RF level shifts as food dries and its dielectric load changes, giving an endpoint without a clock.

new_nodes.label: Detects food load state from reflected RF power
new_nodes.detail: Estimates doneness from the change in load rather than elapsed minutes.

ideas.title: Listening Cavity (Sound-Tracked Doneness)

new_nodes.label: MEMS microphone behind sub-wavelength port
new_nodes.detail: A low-cost MEMS mic behind a sub-wavelength port and shielded PCB hears bubbling, popping and steam hiss.

new_nodes.detail: A tiny on-device classifier maps crackle, bubble and hiss patterns to a cooking-progress estimate.

new_nodes.label: Signals progress with rising tone and completion chime
new_nodes.detail: A continuous pitch climbs with cooking progress and resolves to a chime at doneness, readable by ear.

new_nodes.label: Piezo tone generator
new_nodes.detail: A low-cost piezo element with tone synthesis replaces the spring-hammer bell and can play any cue.

ideas.title: Magnetic Stir Bowl

new_nodes.label: Magnetic stir bar in sealed ferrite core
new_nodes.detail: Non-conductive ferrite sealed in a food-safe bowl base, so it stirs butter, sugar and chocolate without metal arcing.

new_nodes.label: Stirs ingredients while they heat
new_nodes.detail: Keeps butter and chocolate moving so they melt evenly with no pausing to stir.

new_nodes.label: Magnetic coupling through cavity floor
new_nodes.detail: A permanent magnet on the existing motor shaft drives the bowl's stir bar through the cavity floor, replacing the roller ring and coupler.

new_edges.from: Magnetic stir bar in sealed ferrite core
Magnetic stir bar in sealed ferrite core
Magnetic stir bar in sealed ferrite core
Magnetic stir bar in sealed ferrite core
Magnetic stir bar in sealed ferrite core
Magnetic stir bar in sealed ferrite core

ideas.rationale: A magnetic stir bar drives the bowl with no roller ring or coupler, so the user can melt butter and cream sugar in one bowl without stopping to stir, directly serving the M17 prep steps.

ideas.title: Lamp-Broiler

new_nodes.label: Quartz IR broiler tube (300 W)
new_nodes.detail: A quartz-halogen tube at the cavity roof replaces the 20-25 W lamp, glowing orange so the user can watch the cake and browning it.

new_nodes.label: Browns and crisps the cake top
new_nodes.detail: Infrared radiation sets a golden crust on the batter surface, which microwaves alone cannot do.

new_nodes.label: Infrared radiant heating (quartz-halogen emitter)
new_nodes.detail: A hot filament emits infrared that heats surface layers directly, without relying on the RF field.

new_edges.to: Browns and crisps the cake top

new_edges.from: Browns and crisps the cake top
Browns and crisps the cake top

ideas.rationale: Upgrading the interior lamp into a radiant broiler gives the cake a golden, baked top that microwaves alone cannot, so the birthday cake is finished in one cavity.

ideas.title: Swappable Recipe Cam

new_nodes.label: Swappable recipe cam cartridge
new_nodes.detail: A moulded polymer cam disc replaces the 5-step power knob, with lobes that set exact on/off patterns such as 15 s on, 15 s off at low power.

new_nodes.label: Plays preset pulse recipes for prep tasks
new_nodes.detail: Delivers gentle, repeatable pulse patterns for melting butter, softening eggs and melting chocolate.

new_nodes.label: Interchangeable cam-profile encoding
new_nodes.detail: Cam lobe geometry encodes power and timing patterns, so new recipes cost pennies to mould and swap in.

new_edges.to: Plays preset pulse recipes for prep tasks

new_edges.from: Plays preset pulse recipes for prep tasks
Plays preset pulse recipes for prep tasks

ideas.rationale: A swappable recipe cam replaces the power knob with ready-made pulse patterns for melting butter, softening eggs and melting chocolate, serving M17 with one turn and no guesswork.

ideas.title: Bain-Marie Turntable

new_nodes.label: Shallow water bain-marie tray
new_nodes.detail: A microwave-safe dish with a water reservoir replaces the glass turntable, and the bowl sits in the water so food never exceeds the water temperature.

new_nodes.label: Melts butter and chocolate at a capped temperature
new_nodes.detail: The water bath caps food near 100 C, preventing scorching, splatter and superheating.

new_nodes.label: Water as microwave absorber and thermal buffer
new_nodes.detail: Water absorbs 2.45 GHz strongly and stores heat, holding the bowl at a stable, safe temperature.

new_edges.to: Melts butter and chocolate at a capped temperature

new_edges.from: Melts butter and chocolate at a capped temperature
Melts butter and chocolate at a capped temperature

new_edges.to: Water as microwave absorber and thermal buffer

new_edges.from: Water as microwave absorber and thermal buffer
Water as microwave absorber and thermal buffer

ideas.rationale: Turning the turntable into a water bath means melted butter and chocolate cannot scorch, boil over or form hot spots, giving a gentle and repeatable prep step for M17.

ideas.title: Wax-Pellet Melt Sentinel

new_nodes.label: Wax-pellet melt probe (non-metal rod)
new_nodes.detail: A paraffin-filled probe with a plastic rod sits in the butter or eggs, and swappable tips set the melting point, replacing the timer knob.

new_nodes.label: Ends heating at target food state
new_nodes.detail: Cuts power when the ingredient reaches the set temperature, instead of stopping after a guessed time.

new_nodes.label: Wax-pellet thermal actuator (paraffin expansion)
new_nodes.detail: Paraffin expands sharply at its melting point and pushes a rod, with no electronics required.

new_edges.to: Ends heating at target food state

new_edges.from: Ends heating at target food state

ideas.rationale: A wax-pellet probe ends heating when butter or eggs reach the target state instead of after a guessed time, serving the melting and tempering steps of M17.

new_nodes.detail: Gallium-nitride transistors amplify a solid-state oscillator to hundreds of watts with microsecond switching and phase control.

new_nodes.label: Instant-on, continuously variable RF output
new_nodes.detail: Output starts in microseconds and can be set to any level, removing magnetron warm-up and the 30 s duty-cycle wait.

ideas.title: Food-sensing auto-stop (no timer)

new_nodes.label: Waveguide absorption sensor (slot coupler and detector diode)
new_nodes.detail: A small coupling slot in the waveguide samples RF, and a Schottky detector tracks reflected power, which falls as food absorbs energy.

new_nodes.label: Slot-coupled RF sampling and envelope detection
new_nodes.detail: The sampled field is rectified by a diode into a DC level that the controller reads as load absorption.

new_nodes.label: Ends cycle at target heat without a set time
new_nodes.detail: The controller stops heating when absorbed energy reaches the target for the food class, instead of waiting on a timer.

ideas.rationale: Stopping when the food itself reaches target heat removes timer guesswork, so a busy user presses one button and gets a reheat with no overshoot and no second run.

ideas.title: Fixed twin-port field sweeper (no turntable)

new_nodes.label: Twin-port phase-swept RF launcher
new_nodes.detail: Two waveguide-fed launch ports at opposite cavity corners are driven with a time-varying phase offset that sweeps the standing-wave pattern.

new_nodes.label: Two-port phase-offset field steering
new_nodes.detail: The relative phase between two coherent RF feeds shifts hot and cold spots across the cavity with no moving parts.

new_nodes.label: Even heating without mechanical rotation
new_nodes.detail: The electronic sweep fills cold spots in one pass, so food sits still on a flat dish.

ideas.rationale: Electronically swept fields fill the cavity in a single pass with no turntable to wait on, so a reheat finishes sooner and the dish can stay flat and still.

ideas.title: Door-as-bell: spring-pop cycle-end cue

new_nodes.label: Spring-pop latch release cam
new_nodes.detail: The existing lever latch gets a stored-energy cam that, after RF is cut at cycle end, springs the door about 10 mm ajar.

new_nodes.label: Stored-energy spring cam release
new_nodes.detail: A preloaded spring releases a cam that pushes the door hook out of the latch.

new_nodes.label: Visible and tactile end-of-cycle cue
new_nodes.detail: The door opening itself signals completion, visible across the room and felt by blind users.

ideas.rationale: The door springs open the moment a reheat ends, so a busy user grabs the hot plate straight away, and an elderly or distracted user is cued without needing to hear a bell.

ideas.title: Heat-bank phase-change pad for back-to-back reheats

new_nodes.label: Phase-change heat-bank pad
new_nodes.detail: A sealed salt-hydrate pad bonded to the magnetron and transformer melts while absorbing waste heat and releases it slowly, replacing the fan.

new_nodes.label: Latent-heat thermal storage (salt-hydrate phase change)
new_nodes.detail: Melting sodium acetate trihydrate stores hundreds of kJ/kg at a near-constant temperature, with no fan or motor.

new_nodes.label: Back-to-back reheats without cool-down pause
new_nodes.detail: Stored heat keeps the magnetron below its thermal cutout across consecutive cycles, so several plates can be reheated in a row.

ideas.rationale: Banking magnetron waste heat in a melting pad lets consecutive reheats run without the thermal cutout forcing a cool-down pause, so a family can heat several plates in a row.

ideas.title: Solid-State Melt Engine

new_nodes.label: GaN RF amplification at 2.45 GHz
new_nodes.detail: Gallium-nitride transistors amplify microwave signals directly, with no cathode, cavity or high voltage, and can switch between 915 MHz and 2.45 GHz.

new_nodes.label: Low-voltage switch-mode power supply
new_nodes.detail: Mains is converted to about 48 V DC by a compact SMPS, with no step-up transformer or HV doubler.

new_nodes.label: GaN RF amplifier module
new_nodes.detail: Stacked transistor modules summing to 700 W at 2.45 GHz, replacing the magnetron.

new_nodes.label: 48 V SMPS board
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the transformer, capacitor and diode, leaving no lethal stored charge.

new_nodes.label: Continuous 0-100% RF power
new_nodes.detail: Power is set by drive level, so butter melts at a steady 10% with no pulsing.

ideas.rationale: Continuous, low-voltage power lets butter melt at a steady gentle setting with no on/off cycling and no lethal capacitor, which makes melting butter for a cake safer and more predictable.

ideas.title: Magnetic Stir-Melt Floor

new_nodes.label: Magnetic drive through glass
new_nodes.detail: Rotating permanent magnets below a sealed glass floor couple to a magnet in the bowl, so there is no shaft, seal or roller inside the cavity.

new_nodes.label: Under-floor magnetic stirrer
new_nodes.detail: A small motor-driven magnet array under the floor, replacing the turntable motor.

new_nodes.label: Fixed glass floor plate
new_nodes.detail: A flat, crumb-free glass plate replacing the turntable and its roller ring.

new_nodes.label: Sealed PTFE stir bar
new_nodes.detail: A small ferrite magnet sealed in a PTFE capsule and sized to stay below arcing risk.

new_nodes.label: Stirs contents while heating
new_nodes.detail: Active mixing spreads heat evenly and keeps melting butter from separating or spattering.

ideas.rationale: Stirring while the butter melts gives an even, spatter-free melt, and the same bowl can go straight on to creaming sugar, so the prep needs fewer tools.

ideas.title: Butter-Sense Closed Loop

new_nodes.label: Germanium-window IR thermal sensing
new_nodes.detail: An infrared sensor reads the surface temperature through an IR-transparent, RF-blocking germanium window.

new_nodes.label: IR sensor and control board
new_nodes.detail: Reads the contents every second and sets power continuously, replacing the 5-step cam switch and the mechanical timer.

new_nodes.label: Closed-loop temperature hold to recipe target
new_nodes.detail: The user selects 'butter, melted' and the oven holds about 40 °C and stops by itself.

new_edges.to: Closed-loop temperature hold to recipe target

new_edges.from: Closed-loop temperature hold to recipe target
Closed-loop temperature hold to recipe target
Closed-loop temperature hold to recipe target

ideas.rationale: A sensor that holds butter at melting temperature and then stops itself removes the guesswork, and the risk of spatter or scorching, from timed melting for a cake.

ideas.title: Bain-Marie Floor Well

new_nodes.label: Latent-heat water buffer
new_nodes.detail: Water in a shallow well heats by dielectric absorption and caps at 100 °C, so the bowl above cannot overheat.

new_nodes.label: Microwave-heated water well
new_nodes.detail: A shallow dish of water in the cavity floor; the microwaves heat the water, which heats the bowl above by conduction.

new_nodes.label: Gentle conductive melting (no spatter)
new_nodes.detail: Fats melt by conduction from water at or below 100 °C rather than by uneven direct dielectric heating.

ideas.rationale: Melting through a boiling-water bath gives the butter a natural 100 °C ceiling with no spatter and no hot spots, which suits a parent doing prep quickly.

ideas.title: Flush Patch-Antenna Wall

new_nodes.label: Printed patch-antenna array
new_nodes.detail: Flat antenna elements printed on a board, with phase set per element so the fields add evenly across the cavity.

new_nodes.label: Flush patch-antenna panel
new_nodes.detail: A wipe-clean panel set flush in the cavity wall, replacing the waveguide duct and the mica cover.

new_nodes.label: Multi-point phased feeding
new_nodes.detail: Energy enters from many points at once, so a butter block melts evenly rather than from the edges inward.

ideas.rationale: Feeding energy in from many points in the cavity wall melts a butter block evenly and removes the splatter-prone mica cover that needs cleaning after every melt.

ideas.title: Marble Countdown Track

new_nodes.label: Marble countdown track
new_nodes.detail: Clear hopper and channel; each marble is one minute and rolls into a bell cup when cooking ends.

new_nodes.label: Gravity escapement with ball gate
new_nodes.detail: A gate releases one marble at a time under gravity, replacing the motor, cam and clockwork.

new_nodes.label: Shows time left as visible marbles
new_nodes.detail: Marbles remaining in the channel show how much cooking time is left at a glance.

new_nodes.label: One-minute minimum step
new_nodes.detail: Time can only be set in whole-marble steps, so sub-minute cooking is impossible.

new_edges.to: Shows time left as visible marbles

new_edges.from: Shows time left as visible marbles

ideas.rationale: Cooking time becomes a pile of marbles that visibly drains to nothing, so there are no numbers, knobs or clockwork to understand.

ideas.title: Pull-Out Drawer Cooker

new_nodes.label: Pull-out cooking drawer
new_nodes.detail: The cavity slides out toward the user at waist height on a front-loading tray.

new_nodes.label: Slide rail with close-to-start switch
new_nodes.detail: Ball-bearing rails; the final inward travel closes the interlock and starts the magnetron.

new_nodes.label: Starts cooking when drawer is closed
new_nodes.detail: Pushing the drawer in is the start action, and pulling it out stops cooking.

new_nodes.label: Sliding seal must meet leakage limits
new_nodes.detail: The moving choke seal must keep microwave leakage within limits over years of sliding.

new_edges.to: Starts cooking when drawer is closed

new_edges.from: Starts cooking when drawer is closed

new_edges.to: Sliding seal must meet leakage limits

new_edges.from: Sliding seal must meet leakage limits

ideas.rationale: Pushing the drawer in is the one motion that both closes it and starts cooking, so nobody has to bend over a hot door or find a button.

ideas.title: Tap-to-Cook Tagged Meals

new_nodes.label: Tagged meal packaging
new_nodes.detail: A paper-based, microwave-safe NFC inlay on each ready meal stores its cook time and power code.

new_nodes.label: Front tap pad
new_nodes.detail: A flat printed zone on the panel reads the packaged meal when it is held against it, like a contactless card.

new_nodes.label: Passive NFC tag encoding
new_nodes.detail: The tag is powered by the reader's field, needs no battery, and costs cents.

new_nodes.label: Reads cook program from packaging
new_nodes.detail: One tap sets both time and power with no dials or numbers.

new_nodes.label: Plus-30-second fallback button
new_nodes.detail: For untagged food; each press adds 30 seconds at full power.

new_nodes.label: Needs tagged packaging supply
new_nodes.detail: Only tagged meals get a pre-set program, so generic food depends on the fallback.

ideas.rationale: Ready meals arrive pre-programmed, so the user taps the packaged meal on the panel, puts it in, and has nothing to choose.

ideas.title: Steam-Sense One-Press Cook

new_nodes.label: Vent-mounted steam sensor
new_nodes.detail: One cheap humidity or gas sensor in the exhaust louvre detects steam rising from the food.

new_nodes.label: Humidity-curve auto-stop
new_nodes.detail: The shape of the steam curve triggers the end of cooking, with power held at a fixed sensible level.

new_nodes.label: Stops cooking automatically from steam
new_nodes.detail: One press of start; cooking ends when the food stops releasing steam.

new_nodes.label: Dry foods give no steam signal
new_nodes.detail: Bread, pastry and dry meat release too little vapour for the sensor to judge.

new_edges.to: Dry foods give no steam signal

new_edges.from: Dry foods give no steam signal

ideas.rationale: A single cheap steam sensor replaces both dials, so the user presses start once and the oven stops when the food is done.

new_nodes.label: Food-picture rotary dial
new_nodes.detail: A single clicking dial with food pictures instead of numbers; pressing the dial starts cooking.

new_nodes.label: Detent switch with preset lookup
new_nodes.detail: A cam-detent rotary switch selects a stored time and power pair for each picture.

new_nodes.label: Selects cook program from food picture
new_nodes.detail: Turning to a food picture loads that food's time and power automatically.

new_nodes.label: Unlisted foods get no tailored program
new_nodes.detail: Foods not printed on the dial have no preset and rely on a generic program.

Selects cook program from food picture
Selects cook program from food picture

ideas.title: Thermal Eye Thaw Sensor

new_nodes.label: Thermal IR array sensor
new_nodes.detail: Shielded 8x8 thermopile array behind the existing mesh window replaces the 20-25 W lamp and maps cavity surface temperatures.

new_nodes.label: Thermopile infrared imaging
new_nodes.detail: Seebeck thermopile pixels read surface temperature without contact; IR passes through sub-wavelength mesh holes as visible light does.

new_nodes.label: Closed-loop thaw detection
new_nodes.detail: Tracks the coldest zone and cuts or reroutes power when it reaches thawing point, stopping rim cooking.

ideas.rationale: By turning the lamp into a thermal sensor that stops power when the coldest zone thaws, it serves M4 by removing guesswork and rim-cooking during defrost.

ideas.title: Package-as-Program NFC Thaw Tag

new_nodes.label: NFC thaw-tag reader coil
new_nodes.detail: Passive 13.56 MHz reader in the cavity floor, shielded from the magnetron, replaces the timer knob and power cam.

new_nodes.label: Foil-free NFC thaw tag
new_nodes.detail: Printed passive tag (about 3-5 cents) on the package edge, away from cavity walls, encodes weight class and a thaw program.

new_nodes.label: Passive NFC inductive coupling
new_nodes.detail: Tag harvests power from the reader field; no battery, no contact, short-range data exchange.

new_nodes.label: Auto thaw-profile selection
new_nodes.detail: Sets duration and power per food type and weight with zero user input.

ideas.rationale: Letting each frozen pack carry its own thaw program removes dial-guessing so every pack defrosts correctly the first time, serving M4.

ideas.title: 27 MHz RF Plate Thaw

new_nodes.label: 27.12 MHz RF dielectric heating
new_nodes.detail: The ~11 m wavelength gives a smoother field, and RF loss in frozen food is higher than at 2.45 GHz, where ice is nearly transparent.

new_nodes.label: Parallel-plate RF electrodes
new_nodes.detail: Two aluminium plates sandwich the food, replacing the waveguide, mica cover and magnetron antenna.

new_nodes.label: Solid-state 27 MHz RF oscillator
new_nodes.detail: Transistor oscillator on a small board replaces the magnetron, HV transformer, capacitor and diode stack.

new_nodes.label: Volumetric uniform thaw field
new_nodes.detail: Fills the whole load with a smooth field so the frozen core thaws alongside the rims.

new_nodes.label: Electrode arcing at air gaps (RF)
new_nodes.detail: Air pockets between food and plates can spark; plates need dielectric covers and gap control.

ideas.rationale: A 27 MHz plate field heats the whole frozen load more uniformly, so the core thaws alongside the rims and the full defrost completes faster, serving M4.

ideas.title: Static Glycol-Water Edge-Guard Ring

new_nodes.label: Static glycol-water edge-guard ring
new_nodes.detail: Sealed polymer ring of lossy glycol-water gel on a fixed plate surrounds the food; its boiling point is far above water's, so it cannot erupt.

new_nodes.label: Lossy-load edge absorption
new_nodes.detail: The absorbing ring takes power at the hot rims that thaw first, letting the frozen centre catch up.

new_nodes.label: Limits rim overheating during thaw
new_nodes.detail: Stops thawed edges cooking while the core is still frozen.

ideas.rationale: A static edge-absorbing ring draws energy away from the rims that thaw first, letting the frozen centre catch up and serving M4 with no moving parts.

ideas.title: Stepless Phase-Angle Thaw Dial

new_nodes.label: Triac phase-angle power controller
new_nodes.detail: A cheap triac on the HV transformer primary gives stepless power; below about 40% power a short pulse train takes over, because magnetrons struggle at very low anode voltage.

new_nodes.label: Zero-cross phase-angle firing
new_nodes.detail: The triac fires at a set angle each half-cycle, so average power is continuous rather than a 30 s on/off duty cycle.

new_nodes.label: Stepless low-power thaw
new_nodes.detail: Gentle continuous power holds the rims below cooking temperature while the core thaws.

ideas.rationale: Stepless low power lets the oven hold the rims below cooking temperature while the core thaws, serving M4 without the stress of cam-switch cycling.

new_nodes.label: Micro CMOS camera module with IR-cut filter
new_nodes.detail: Under 0.3 W, mounted behind a sub-wavelength aperture; streams the cavity to the door display or a phone.

new_nodes.label: Pulsed white LED illuminator
new_nodes.detail: About 0.2 W, flashes only during image capture, so the cavity is lit for milliseconds instead of the whole cook.

new_nodes.label: Low-power on-demand cavity view
new_nodes.detail: The user sees the food on request while the cook runs, with no continuous light load.

ideas.rationale: Replacing the 20-25 W incandescent lamp, which turns nearly all its power into heat, with a sub-watt camera and a pulsed LED cuts the energy spent on viewing by over 90 percent and removes bulb-replacement waste.

ideas.title: Done-sensing controller replaces the timer and power cams

new_nodes.label: Humidity and VOC gas sensor in the exhaust path
new_nodes.detail: Tracks steam and volatile release from the food, giving the doneness signal the cam timer never had.

new_nodes.label: Microcontroller control board with power-modulation firmware
new_nodes.detail: Sub-watt digital controller that sets duty cycle continuously from the sensor curve and ends the cook automatically.

new_nodes.label: Gas and humidity food-state estimation
new_nodes.detail: Uses steam and volatile release curves to infer doneness and stop at the target point.

new_nodes.label: Stops heating at sensed doneness
new_nodes.detail: The magnetron runs only until the food is ready, not for a guessed time.

ideas.title: Solid-state GaN phased amplifier replaces the magnetron and HV transformer chain

new_nodes.label: GaN RF power amplifier array (2.45 GHz, multi-channel)
new_nodes.detail: Low-voltage solid-state transistors generate the microwaves in place of the magnetron tube, with per-channel phase control.

new_nodes.label: Universal low-voltage switched-mode PSU (about 50 V DC)
new_nodes.detail: High-frequency converter with 90-265 V universal input that performs the mains-to-DC function without a 50 Hz step-up transformer, HV capacitor or diode.

new_nodes.label: Ferrite circulator with reflected-power recycle loop
new_nodes.detail: Routes energy reflected from a mismatched load into a second amplifier channel instead of wasting it.

new_nodes.label: Gallium nitride RF power transistors
new_nodes.detail: High-efficiency microwave transistors rooted in RF engineering.

new_nodes.label: Continuously variable, phase-steered RF power
new_nodes.detail: Power is set smoothly and can be aimed at cold spots without a rotating tray.

new_nodes.label: Higher RF semiconductor BOM than a magnetron
new_nodes.detail: GaN transistors and an amplifier array raise cost and pressure the low-price segment.

ideas.rationale: Solid-state amplifiers remove the 4 kV transformer and magnetron heater losses, let every watt be steered toward the food, and reclaim reflected energy, so far less of the mains draw is lost as heat.

ideas.title: Waste-heat plenum replaces the cooling fan and exhaust louvres

new_nodes.label: Passive sealed heat-pipe thermal bus
new_nodes.detail: Copper heat pipes carry magnetron and transformer waste heat with no pump or fan, so the electronics cool passively.

new_nodes.label: Finned cavity air-preheat plenum
new_nodes.detail: A warm finned plate behind the cavity heats the air and cooking space with recovered waste heat; louvres shrink to a steam-only vent.

new_nodes.label: Reuses magnetron waste heat for cavity warming
new_nodes.detail: Heat that is normally vented now pre-warms the cavity and the food.

new_nodes.label: Two-phase heat-pipe heat transport
new_nodes.detail: Phase-change heat transport that needs no power, rooted in thermal engineering.

new_edges.to: Reuses magnetron waste heat for cavity warming

new_edges.from: Reuses magnetron waste heat for cavity warming

ideas.rationale: Recovering the roughly 35-40 percent of input energy that a magnetron oven currently vents as waste heat, and cooling the electronics passively, removes the fan's own power draw and gives the cavity free pre-heat.

ideas.title: Patterned low-emissivity window keeps cavity heat in

new_nodes.label: Patterned low-emissivity screen window
new_nodes.detail: A sub-wavelength conductive film grid that is visible-transparent, reflects mid-infrared heat back into the cavity, and screens microwaves like the mesh does.

new_nodes.label: Low-emissivity thin-film coating on sub-wavelength grid
new_nodes.detail: A thin conductive film stack that reflects thermal infrared while passing visible light.

new_nodes.label: Retains cavity heat during long cooks and reheats
new_nodes.detail: The food's own infrared is reflected back through the window, so less heat radiates out through the door.

new_nodes.label: Coating wear from steam and cleaning
new_nodes.detail: Thin films degrade under steam, grease and abrasive cleaning, which can shorten window life.

new_nodes.label: GaN solid-state RF amplifier array
new_nodes.detail: Tiled gallium-nitride amplifier modules on one 48 V PCB replace the magnetron, HV transformer, capacitor, diode and waveguide.

ideas.title: Susceptor ceramic plate replaces the turntable

new_nodes.label: Cavity vapour sensor pair (MOX gas + humidity)

new_nodes.label: Vapour-based food-state sensing

new_nodes.label: Closed-loop end-point cooking

ideas.title: Solid-state GaN RF amplifier replaces magnetron and HV chain

new_nodes.label: GaN HEMT solid-state RF power amplification at 2.45 GHz
new_nodes.detail: Gallium-nitride transistors amplify a 2.45 GHz signal directly from a low-voltage DC rail, with no cathode and no 4 kV supply.

new_nodes.label: Solid-state RF amplifier module array
new_nodes.detail: Several GaN modules combine to about 700 W, with drive level set continuously in real time, replacing the magnetron tube.

new_nodes.label: 48 V DC switch-mode power supply
new_nodes.detail: High-frequency ferrite-core SMPS replaces the iron-core HV transformer, voltage-doubler capacitor and diode.

new_nodes.label: Delivers continuously variable RF power
new_nodes.detail: Output follows the food load continuously, so no energy is lost to on/off duty-cycling or magnetron start-up.

new_nodes.label: Converts mains to low-voltage DC for RF amplifiers
new_nodes.detail: A single high-frequency conversion stage replaces mains-to-4 kV conversion.

new_edges.to: GaN HEMT solid-state RF power amplification at 2.45 GHz
GaN HEMT solid-state RF power amplification at 2.45 GHz

new_edges.from: GaN HEMT solid-state RF power amplification at 2.45 GHz

new_edges.to: Converts mains to low-voltage DC for RF amplifiers

new_edges.from: Converts mains to low-voltage DC for RF amplifiers

ideas.rationale: Continuously modulated solid-state RF removes the magnetron's cathode warm-up, its on/off duty-cycle losses and the lossy iron-core HV transformer, so more mains energy reaches the food.

ideas.title: Ambient-light pipe replaces the 25 W cavity lamp

new_nodes.label: Ambient-light harvesting via acrylic light pipe
new_nodes.detail: Room light is collected at the fascia and piped into the cavity through a dielectric light guide, with zero electrical input.

new_nodes.label: Fascia light collector and light pipe
new_nodes.detail: A molded PMMA collector and 5 mm guide route room light through the door mesh; a 0.1 W LED on the same pipe covers dark kitchens. The rod is far below dielectric cut-off at 2.45 GHz, so it leaks negligibly.

new_nodes.label: Lights the cavity with zero electrical power
new_nodes.detail: Visibility comes from the kitchen itself, so the lamp's 20-25 W draw, its heat and its burnout risk disappear.

new_edges.from: Fascia light collector and light pipe
Fascia light collector and light pipe
new_edges.to: Ambient-light harvesting via acrylic light pipe

new_edges.from: Ambient-light harvesting via acrylic light pipe
Fascia light collector and light pipe
new_edges.to: Lights the cavity with zero electrical power

new_edges.from: Lights the cavity with zero electrical power
Fascia light collector and light pipe
Lights the cavity with zero electrical power

ideas.rationale: A passive light pipe that harvests room light removes the lamp's 20-25 W draw from every cook, cutting energy per cycle while keeping the cavity visible.

ideas.title: Heat-pipe and phase-change thermal battery replaces cooling fan

new_nodes.label: Heat-pipe thermosiphon with phase-change thermal storage
new_nodes.detail: Sealed heat pipes carry magnetron and transformer heat to a finned stack, and a paraffin PCM block buffers the peaks.

ideas.title: Tray-as-Dial: turn the glass plate to set the time

new_nodes.label: Tray time-dial
new_nodes.detail: Grip-ringed glass tray: turn it by hand with the door open. Its angle sets 0-30 min (about 1 min per 12 degrees), then the turntable motor takes over.

new_nodes.label: Magnetic angle encoder
new_nodes.detail: A magnet ring under the tray and a Hall sensor in the roller ring read tray angle to about 1 degree (about 5 s), replacing the cam switch.

new_nodes.label: Sets cooking time by turning the tray
new_nodes.detail: Duration comes straight from the tray's rotation, the same motion people already use on a lazy susan.

new_edges.to: Sets cooking time by turning the tray

new_edges.from: Sets cooking time by turning the tray
Sets cooking time by turning the tray

ideas.rationale: Setting time by turning a plate is a motion everyone already knows, so there is nothing to read, learn or translate.

ideas.title: Picture-Preset Pad replaces the power knob

new_nodes.label: Three-picture preset pad
new_nodes.detail: Raised tactile keys with embossed food pictures (Drink, Frozen, Melt) replace the 5-step knob. Each key selects a pre-tuned power profile, with no numbers to read.

new_nodes.label: Embossed membrane switch with profile table
new_nodes.detail: Sealed polymer membrane keys with tactile bumps. The controller maps each key to a stored duty-cycle table tuned for that food.

new_nodes.label: Chooses heating profile by food picture
new_nodes.detail: Tapping a food picture applies the right power and on/off pattern, so the user never meets the duty cycle.

ideas.rationale: Recognising a picture of your food is the simplest possible choice, so no power level has to be understood to get the right result.

ideas.title: Pull-Out Drawer Cavity replaces the hinged door

new_nodes.label: Pull-out drawer cavity
new_nodes.detail: The cavity slides out on telescopic runners. Pull the grip to load and push to close, with no swing arc, no hinges and no release button.

new_nodes.label: Telescopic runner with detent latch
new_nodes.detail: Ball-bearing runners with a spring detent that holds the drawer shut and clicks when pushed home.

new_nodes.label: Sliding quarter-wave choke rim
new_nodes.detail: A choke rim carried on the drawer front keeps RF leakage blocked across the whole slide travel.

new_nodes.label: Opens the cavity with a straight pull
new_nodes.detail: One straight pull gives access, the same motion as a kitchen drawer, with nothing to swing out of the way.

new_nodes.label: Choke rim wear over repeated slides
new_nodes.detail: Sliding contact can scuff the rim or trap food debris, slowly weakening the RF seal.

new_nodes.label: Clear front space for drawer travel
new_nodes.detail: The drawer needs about the cavity depth of clear counter in front, which works against the small-footprint need.

ideas.title: Rising Done Tab replaces the bell

new_nodes.label: Rising done tab
new_nodes.detail: A spring-loaded tab pops 15 mm out of the control panel at the end of cooking and stays up until pressed back down.

new_nodes.label: Spring pop-up pin on cam end-stop
new_nodes.detail: The timer cam's end position releases a spring plunger, so the tab rises silently instead of striking a bell.

new_nodes.label: Signals end of cooking by a visible rising tab
new_nodes.detail: Seen from across the kitchen and felt by touch, so it works for people who are deaf, visually impaired or in noisy kitchens.

ideas.title: Steam-Stop Reheat: the food decides when it is done

new_nodes.label: Steam-sensing cutoff
new_nodes.detail: A small metal-oxide humidity sensor in the vent path watches for steam leaving the food and ends reheating when steaming starts.

new_nodes.label: Metal-oxide steam sensing
new_nodes.detail: A ceramic metal-oxide element whose resistance drops as vapour rises. The controller reads this as 'food is hot'.

new_nodes.label: Ends reheating when food starts to steam
new_nodes.detail: One Reheat key replaces the countdown, so the user never sets a time and the food signals when it is ready.

new_nodes.label: Steam signal weak for cold or frozen food
new_nodes.detail: No vapour is produced until the food warms, so sensing alone cannot judge frozen-food cycles.

ideas.title: Steam Stop: the microwave ends itself when the food steams

new_nodes.label: Vent-louvre steam sensor
new_nodes.detail: Cheap metal-oxide gas sensor tucked into the existing vent louvres; rising steam ends cooking and replaces the timer dial.

new_nodes.label: MOX gas/humidity sensing
new_nodes.detail: Resistive metal-oxide sensor whose resistance falls as steam rises, read by a simple comparator circuit.

new_nodes.label: Chemical & environmental sensing
new_nodes.detail: Gas, humidity and vapour detection for appliance control.

new_nodes.label: Stops cooking when food is steaming hot
new_nodes.detail: Ends the cycle on the food's own cue, so the user presses one Start button and sets no number.

new_nodes.label: Steam-poor foods may never trigger the stop
new_nodes.detail: Dry foods such as bread or pastry give little steam, so a fallback safety timeout is needed.

new_edges.to: Stops cooking when food is steaming hot

new_edges.from: Stops cooking when food is steaming hot
Stops cooking when food is steaming hot

new_edges.to: Steam-poor foods may never trigger the stop

ideas.rationale: Replacing a timer that must be guessed with one Start press and a stop triggered by the food's own steam leaves the elderly user with no numbers to read or set.

ideas.title: Packet Card: the meal's sleeve is the power knob

new_nodes.label: Card slot with notch-reader
new_nodes.detail: Slot in the control panel where the meal card is pushed in; spring feeler pins read its notches and set the duty cycle mechanically.

new_nodes.label: Notched meal card
new_nodes.detail: Stiff card printed on the frozen-meal sleeve whose notch pattern encodes the heating profile for that food.

new_nodes.label: Mechanical notch-code reading
new_nodes.detail: Feeler pins drop into card notches and drive the existing duty-cycle cam, with no electronics required.

new_nodes.label: Printed notch-code cards
new_nodes.detail: Notches stamped into paperboard during packaging at near-zero marginal cost.

new_nodes.label: Sets food-specific heating profile
new_nodes.detail: Chooses the on/off ratio for the inserted food, replacing the five-step numeric power knob.

new_nodes.label: Cards can be lost or left at home
new_nodes.detail: Without the card the oven needs a default profile or a plain reheat setting.

new_edges.to: Cards can be lost or left at home

ideas.rationale: The packaging carries the setting, so the user slides in the card that came with their dinner and never has to understand power levels.

ideas.title: Cake Dome: the door becomes a lift-off cloche and lowering it starts cooking

new_nodes.label: Lift-off glass dome
new_nodes.detail: Lightweight microwave-transparent dome that lifts straight off a base plate; lowering it onto the base starts cooking and lifting it stops.

new_nodes.label: Quarter-wave choke rim seal
new_nodes.detail: Groove around the dome rim presents a high-impedance path so microwaves stay inside without a hinge or latch.

new_nodes.label: Hall-effect seating interlock
new_nodes.detail: Magnet and sensor pair in the base confirms the dome is fully seated before the magnetron may run.

new_nodes.label: Gives cavity access by lift and lower
new_nodes.detail: One vertical motion opens or closes the cavity and doubles as the start command.

new_nodes.label: Dome weight and steam burns at lift-off
new_nodes.detail: A large dome lifted from hot food can be heavy for weak wrists and releases a steam burst.

new_edges.to: Gives cavity access by lift and lower

new_edges.from: Gives cavity access by lift and lower
Gives cavity access by lift and lower

new_edges.to: Dome weight and steam burns at lift-off

ideas.rationale: Lifting a dome straight up and lowering it to start replaces a swinging door, a release button and a separate start press with one intuitive motion.

ideas.title: Ring-to-Open: the bell also unlocks the door

new_nodes.label: Bell-triggered door eject
new_nodes.detail: The end-of-cook bell striker also trips a spring that pops the door ajar about 2 cm, so the finished food presents itself.

new_nodes.label: Bell-coupled spring latch release
new_nodes.detail: The bell striker shares one cam with the latch lever, so ringing and unlatching happen in a single mechanical motion.

new_nodes.label: Presents finished food at end of cooking
new_nodes.detail: The door opens by itself when the bell rings, removing the search for a release button.

new_nodes.label: Steam and heat burst when the door pops
new_nodes.detail: An ajar door releases a jet of hot steam at face height.

new_edges.to: Presents finished food at end of cooking

new_edges.from: Presents finished food at end of cooking

new_edges.to: Steam and heat burst when the door pops

ideas.rationale: The machine announces the finished food and opens itself, so an elderly user never has to find or press a release button to get the food out.

ideas.title: Sand-Glass Cook: flip the hourglass and cook until the sand runs out

new_nodes.label: Flip-to-cook sand-glass
new_nodes.detail: Transparent hourglass on the front; flipping it closes a microswitch, and when the sand runs out power is cut and the bell rings.

new_nodes.label: Gravity-flow timing
new_nodes.detail: Sand falling through a calibrated orifice sets duration with no motor, gears or electronics.

new_nodes.label: Shows cooking time as falling sand
new_nodes.detail: Progress is visible at a glance, so no numbers need reading or setting.

new_nodes.label: Sand flow drifts with humidity and wear
new_nodes.detail: Grain moisture and orifice wear shift timing, so cartridges need periodic replacement.

new_edges.to: Shows cooking time as falling sand

new_edges.from: Shows cooking time as falling sand
Shows cooking time as falling sand

new_edges.to: Sand flow drifts with humidity and wear

ideas.rationale: Watching sand fall gives a visible, numberless countdown and a single flip to start, so the user needs no understanding of timers at all.

ideas.title: Solid-State Butter Dial

new_nodes.label: GaN solid-state RF amplifier at 2.45 GHz
new_nodes.detail: Transistor-based RF source giving continuous, adjustable output from a low-voltage supply.

new_nodes.label: GaN RF amplifier module
new_nodes.detail: One low-voltage PCB replaces the magnetron tube, HV transformer, HV capacitor and rectifier diode.

new_nodes.label: Continuously variable microwave power
new_nodes.detail: Holds a steady gentle level (e.g. 5-10 percent) so butter melts evenly without on/off surges.

new_edges.to: GaN solid-state RF amplifier at 2.45 GHz

new_edges.from: GaN solid-state RF amplifier at 2.45 GHz

ideas.rationale: Replacing the magnetron chain with continuously variable solid-state power lets a baker melt butter gently and evenly, avoiding the scorching and splatter of full-power bursts.

ideas.title: Susceptor Bakestone Turntable

new_nodes.label: Graphite-loaded ceramic susceptor
new_nodes.detail: Microwave-absorbing ceramic that heats itself to 200 °C or more and radiates dry heat.

new_nodes.label: Susceptor bakestone turntable
new_nodes.detail: Glass tray swapped for a susceptor plate that browns the underside of cakes and warms tins by conduction.

new_nodes.label: Dry surface browning by conductive heat
new_nodes.detail: Gives cake layers a golden, set crust and a dry, oven-like base.

new_edges.to: Dry surface browning by conductive heat

new_edges.from: Dry surface browning by conductive heat
Dry surface browning by conductive heat

ideas.rationale: A susceptor turntable gives a birthday cake the golden, set crust a microwave normally cannot produce, while also warming the baking tin and butter by conduction.

ideas.title: Melt-Point Plug Timer

new_nodes.label: Phase-change melt-point plug (food-grade wax)
new_nodes.detail: Wax plug tuned to butter's 32-35 °C melting range that slumps once the butter is liquid.

new_nodes.label: Piezo disc acoustic transducer
new_nodes.detail: Ceramic disc that produces a clear tone or short melody from a low-voltage drive.

new_nodes.label: Butter-melt plug and spring plunger
new_nodes.detail: Plug sits in the bowl base; when it slumps, a spring plunger trips the interlock and ends the cycle.

new_nodes.label: Piezo birthday chime
new_nodes.detail: Piezo buzzer replacing the spring-hammer bell with a short birthday chime.

new_nodes.label: Ends cook on ingredient state, not elapsed time
new_nodes.detail: Stops heating when the butter has melted, so the baker never counts minutes or scorches it.

new_edges.to: Ends cook on ingredient state, not elapsed time

new_edges.from: Ends cook on ingredient state, not elapsed time
Ends cook on ingredient state, not elapsed time
Ends cook on ingredient state, not elapsed time

ideas.rationale: Ending the cycle when the butter itself turns liquid, and announcing it with a birthday chime, removes the guesswork from melting butter for a cake.

ideas.title: Waste-Heat Proofing Loop

new_nodes.label: Passive heat-pipe thermal transport
new_nodes.detail: Sealed copper pipe with working fluid moves heat by evaporation and condensation, with no moving parts.

new_nodes.label: Magnetron heat-pipe radiator
new_nodes.detail: Finned radiator in the cavity wall carries magnetron and transformer waste heat into the cooking space.

new_nodes.label: Gentle warm-air holding for softening butter and eggs
new_nodes.detail: Keeps the cavity at about 35-40 °C so butter and eggs reach room temperature.

new_nodes.label: Radiator reduces usable cavity volume
new_nodes.detail: The finned radiator occupies part of the roughly 20 L cavity.

new_edges.to: Gentle warm-air holding for softening butter and eggs

new_edges.from: Gentle warm-air holding for softening butter and eggs
Gentle warm-air holding for softening butter and eggs

ideas.rationale: Recycling magnetron waste heat into a gentle warm-air mode lets a baker soften butter and eggs in the same appliance, saving prep time and energy without an extra heating element.

ideas.title: Magnetic Paddle Mixer

new_nodes.label: Non-contact magnetic gearing
new_nodes.detail: Permanent-magnet coupling transmits torque through a sealed wall with no shaft seal.

new_nodes.label: Magnetic drive coupling
new_nodes.detail: Magnet ring under the cavity floor spins an internal stirrer, replacing the roller ring and coupler.

new_nodes.label: PBT paddle mixer hub
new_nodes.detail: Microwave-transparent paddle that turns inside the bowl, stirring food and disturbing standing waves.

new_nodes.label: In-bowl stirring of batter and melted butter
new_nodes.detail: Blends melted butter with sugar and eggs in the same bowl that is heated.

new_edges.to: In-bowl stirring of batter and melted butter

new_edges.from: In-bowl stirring of batter and melted butter
In-bowl stirring of batter and melted butter

ideas.rationale: A rotating paddle in the heating bowl lets a baker melt butter and whisk in sugar and eggs in one vessel, so the appliance handles the mixing a birthday cake needs.

ideas.title: Solid-state RF thaw module

new_nodes.label: GaN solid-state RF amplifier
new_nodes.detail: Transistor RF amplifier on a low-voltage DC rail generates 2.45 GHz with no vacuum tube, filament or 4 kV supply.

new_nodes.label: GaN RF amplifier module
new_nodes.detail: Small heatsinked amplifier board that replaces the magnetron, HV transformer, HV capacitor and rectifier diode.

new_nodes.label: Continuous variable RF power
new_nodes.detail: Power adjustable smoothly from 5 to 700 W with no on/off cycling, so thawing becomes a steady low-power soak.

ideas.rationale: A low-voltage solid-state source lets frozen food thaw in a gentle continuous soak with no lethal capacitor and no duty-cycle pulsing, which makes defrost safer and cheaper to build.

ideas.title: Phased-array thaw walls

new_nodes.label: Phased-array printed patch antennas
new_nodes.detail: Etched copper patches bonded behind the cavity wall steer the RF beam electronically by changing the phase of each patch.

new_nodes.label: Electronically steered antenna array
new_nodes.detail: Flat antenna sheet on a small phase network that replaces the waveguide, mica cover, turntable tray, roller ring and motor.

new_nodes.label: Electronic field sweep
new_nodes.detail: Beam angle sweeps across the cavity many times per second so cold centres and warm edges average out.

ideas.rationale: Steering the field electronically with no moving parts averages out standing-wave hot and cold spots, so frozen centres thaw as fast as the edges, which is a leading cause of failed defrosts.

ideas.title: Self-sensing thaw endpoint

new_nodes.label: Loss-tangent sensing via anode current
new_nodes.detail: Ice melting into water shifts dielectric loss, which appears as a measurable change in magnetron anode current and reflected power.

new_nodes.label: Thaw-state controller
new_nodes.detail: Firmware reads the sensed signature and steps power up or down, replacing the 5-step cam switch and manual time or weight guessing.

new_nodes.label: Automatic thaw-endpoint detection
new_nodes.detail: Drops to a gentle finish and stops the moment the block turns from ice to water, with no weight or time entry.

ideas.rationale: A parent presses one button and the oven senses the ice-to-water transition itself and stops at the right moment, removing the guesswork that leads to cooked edges and still-frozen centres.

ideas.title: Salted ohmic electrode thaw tray

new_nodes.label: Ohmic heating at mains frequency
new_nodes.detail: Current passed through salted food heats it volumetrically by ionic conduction, with no radio waves and no dielectric dependence.

new_nodes.label: Brine-wetted electrode tray
new_nodes.detail: Two stainless plates in a tray with salt-brine pads that bootstrap conduction through the frozen block, replacing the magnetron and waveguide.

new_nodes.label: Volumetric conduction thaw without RF
new_nodes.detail: Heats the whole block at once through its ionic content, so there is no radiation to shield and no standing-wave hot spots.

ideas.rationale: Passing a gentle current straight through a salted frozen block thaws the whole mass at once with no radiation and no magnetron, so defrost becomes faster, more even and much cheaper to manufacture.

ideas.title: Latent-heat thaw plate

new_nodes.label: Latent-heat plateau thermostat
new_nodes.detail: Sodium sulfate decahydrate (Glauber's salt) melts near 32 °C, so absorbed microwave energy goes into melting rather than raising temperature.

new_nodes.label: Phase-change thaw plate
new_nodes.detail: Sealed plate in the cavity floor that holds the food-contact temperature at the melt point while the magnetron runs flat-out.

new_nodes.label: Full-power thaw with self-limiting temperature
new_nodes.detail: Constant full power with no duty cycling, while the plate clamps the food-contact temperature so the outside cannot overheat.

ideas.rationale: Banking microwave energy as latent heat in a salt plate lets the magnetron run at full power while the food thaws gently and evenly against a self-limiting temperature, replacing the slow on-off cycling that makes defrost uneven.

ideas.title: Weigh, Close, Done

new_nodes.label: Turntable load-cell pad
new_nodes.detail: Strain-gauge weigh pad under the glass turntable reads food mass and replaces the timer dial.

new_nodes.label: Mass-to-time lookup curve
new_nodes.detail: Factory-calibrated table maps measured mass and food class to a cook time on a cheap microcontroller.

new_nodes.label: Infers cook time from food mass
new_nodes.detail: Sets the duration automatically, so there is no number to read, set or misjudge.

new_nodes.label: Auto-starts when door closes on a loaded plate
new_nodes.detail: Closing the door on a plate with food on it begins cooking, so no start button is needed.

new_edges.to: Infers cook time from food mass
Auto-starts when door closes on a loaded plate

new_edges.from: Infers cook time from food mass
Infers cook time from food mass
Auto-starts when door closes on a loaded plate

ideas.rationale: The user's only job is to put food on the plate and close the door, so there is no setting to learn at all.

ideas.title: Picture Plate Power

new_nodes.label: Three-picture food selector
new_nodes.detail: A single switch with three large pictograms (drop for drinks and soup, plate for leftovers, snowflake for frozen) replaces the 5-step power knob.

new_nodes.label: Food-type duty-cycle presets
new_nodes.detail: Firmware maps each picture to a fixed on/off duty pattern, so percentages are hidden from the user.

new_nodes.label: Matches heating profile to food type
new_nodes.detail: Chooses power and cycling by recognising the food rather than reading a power level.

new_edges.to: Matches heating profile to food type

new_edges.from: Matches heating profile to food type
Matches heating profile to food type

ideas.rationale: Users choose by recognising their food instead of interpreting '3' or '60 percent', so no concept of power has to be learned.

ideas.title: Door Comes To You

new_nodes.label: Full-face magnetic pop latch
new_nodes.detail: The whole door face becomes the control: a light press anywhere pops it open, replacing the small release button and lever.

new_nodes.label: Magnetic detent with spring pop
new_nodes.detail: A permanent magnet holds the door shut, and a small spring or solenoid pops it open on release.

new_nodes.label: Pops door open at cycle end
new_nodes.detail: When the magnetron stops, the door eases open a few centimetres so the user never hunts for a button.

new_edges.to: Pops door open at cycle end

new_edges.from: Pops door open at cycle end
Pops door open at cycle end

ideas.rationale: The oven delivers the door to the user at the end of cooking, and the whole face is the only control, so there is nothing to find, press or remember.

ideas.title: Drawer, Not Door

new_nodes.label: Pull-out cavity drawer
new_nodes.detail: The cavity and turntable slide out on runners like a bread drawer; the drawer front, with its mesh window, is the only handle.

new_nodes.label: Quarter-wave choke seal
new_nodes.detail: A quarter-wavelength choke groove on the sliding flange keeps 2.45 GHz energy inside while the drawer moves.

new_nodes.label: Slides cavity out to counter height
new_nodes.detail: Brings food to the user at counter height with no swing arc, no hinge and no reaching up to a hot door.

new_edges.to: Slides cavity out to counter height

new_edges.from: Slides cavity out to counter height
Slides cavity out to counter height

ideas.rationale: Pulling a drawer out at counter height is a motion everyone already knows, so the hinge, swing arc and hot-door hazards disappear without any instructions.

ideas.title: Sunrise Ring

new_nodes.label: Sunrise progress ring
new_nodes.detail: An LED ring around the door frame shows a lit arc that shrinks as time runs down and glows green when done, replacing the bell signal.

new_nodes.label: Countdown-driven LED ring drive
new_nodes.detail: A low-power LED driver scales the lit arc from the cook counter, sharing the timer's microcontroller.

new_nodes.label: Shows remaining time at a glance
new_nodes.detail: Progress is read as a shrinking arc, so no numbers and no hearing are needed.

new_edges.to: Shows remaining time at a glance
Shows remaining time at a glance

new_edges.from: Shows remaining time at a glance

ideas.rationale: Users see how much time is left as a shrinking arc and know the food is done when the ring turns green, so no number, sound or learned convention is needed.

ideas.title: Thermal Eye

new_nodes.label: Ceiling thermopile array (8x8 IR sensor)
new_nodes.detail: Mounted outside the cavity behind a 1 mm hole: infrared gets through, microwaves do not. Replaces the bulb.

new_nodes.label: Thermopile infrared sensing
new_nodes.detail: Thermocouple arrays turn incoming infrared into voltage, with no filament and no moving parts.

new_nodes.label: Infrared sensing & thermography
new_nodes.detail: Measuring surface temperature from emitted infrared radiation.

new_nodes.label: Heat-map of cold spots
new_nodes.detail: Shows unheated zones on a phone or door strip so the user sees when food is evenly done.

ideas.rationale: By turning the window into a heat sensor, the user can see which parts of the food are still cold and know when it is evenly done instead of guessing from a bulb's glow.

ideas.title: Popcorn Ear

new_nodes.label: MEMS microphone with sound classifier
new_nodes.detail: A sub-dollar mic and tiny chip listen for pops, bubbles and sizzle, then trigger a piezo beep in place of the spring hammer.

new_nodes.label: MEMS acoustic sensing with on-chip classification
new_nodes.detail: A microphone plus microcontroller recognises the sound pattern of each food type.

new_nodes.label: Detects fading food sound as doneness
new_nodes.detail: Popping slows and sizzling fades as food finishes, so the food itself reports completion.

new_edges.to: MEMS acoustic sensing with on-chip classification

new_edges.from: MEMS acoustic sensing with on-chip classification

new_edges.to: Detects fading food sound as doneness

new_edges.from: Detects fading food sound as doneness
Detects fading food sound as doneness

ideas.rationale: The food's own popping and sizzle report its progress, so the user is alerted by what the food is actually doing rather than by a timer's guess.

ideas.title: Reflected-Power Pulse

new_nodes.label: Reflectometer trace on magnetron feed
new_nodes.detail: A printed directional coupler reads reflected RF power, so the food's load shows in the reflection curve with no extra sensor.

new_nodes.label: Food-type preset dial
new_nodes.detail: Dial picks soup, reheat, popcorn or frozen veg instead of minutes, with no cam, spring or motor.

new_nodes.label: Directional-coupler reflectometry
new_nodes.detail: Samples forward and reflected 2.45 GHz power to track the food's electrical load.

new_nodes.label: Ends cooking at the load-change knee
new_nodes.detail: Stops when the reflection curve kinks, which marks the food reaching its target state.

new_edges.to: Ends cooking at the load-change knee

new_edges.from: Ends cooking at the load-change knee
Ends cooking at the load-change knee
Ends cooking at the load-change knee

new_nodes.detail: One rotary dial with five detents, each printed with a food picture (mug, popcorn bag, dinner plate, frozen block, ice cube).

new_nodes.label: Multi-lobe cam with factory presets
new_nodes.detail: Each detent rotates a cam lobe that fixes both duration and on/off ratio, so the user never reads or sets numbers.

new_nodes.label: Selects a cooking program by picture
new_nodes.detail: One recognisable choice replaces the separate time and power decisions.

ideas.title: Door Says Done

new_nodes.label: Spring-popped door
new_nodes.detail: At timer zero the cam trips the latch lever and a preloaded spring pushes the door open about 3 cm, where it stays until lifted.

new_nodes.label: End-of-cook bell (retired)
new_nodes.detail: Sounds a bell at timer zero; the base product's only end-of-cook cue.

new_nodes.detail: A visible, physical cue that needs no hearing, reading, or memory of a beep.

ideas.rationale: Cooking ends with the door visibly opening, so an older user with poor hearing or memory knows the food is ready without interpreting any sound.

ideas.title: Pot-Lid Access

new_nodes.label: Top-lift lid
new_nodes.detail: A one-piece lid lifts straight up by a finger notch and stays open on its own, replacing the front door, hinges and push button.

new_nodes.label: Gas-spring counterweight
new_nodes.detail: An off-the-shelf gas strut, as used in car tailgates, balances the lid so a light lift holds it open.

new_nodes.label: Quarter-wave choke seal
new_nodes.detail: A metal choke channel around the rim blocks microwave leakage without a mesh window or latch.

new_nodes.label: Opens cavity by lifting, no button

ideas.title: Steam-Stop: The Food Ends the Cook

new_nodes.label: Steam-vent bimetal trip
new_nodes.detail: A small bimetal disc in the vent path bends when the steam plume reaches it and cuts the magnetron circuit, so there is no timer to set.

new_nodes.label: Bimetallic steam-flow actuation
new_nodes.detail: A snap-action bimetal converts the heat of the steam plume into a mechanical switch trip.

new_nodes.label: Ends cooking when food starts to steam
new_nodes.detail: A food-state cue replaces a guessed duration; best for leftovers, drinks and vegetables, with crisping foods needing a timer fallback.

ideas.title: Plate Goes Down, No Turntable

new_nodes.label: Glass turntable
new_nodes.detail: The base product's rotating glass plate and drive ring, which must be seated correctly over the drive coupling (now retired).

new_nodes.label: Fixed ceramic plate
new_nodes.detail: A plain, flat ceramic dish sits on the cavity floor, with nothing to align, reseat or wash around a drive ring.

new_nodes.label: Mode-stirrer vane
new_nodes.detail: A slow-turning metal vane at the cavity wall mixes the microwave field so the food need not rotate.

new_nodes.label: Motorised reflector vane
new_nodes.detail: A small motor drives a reflector vane that reshapes the RF field inside the cavity.

new_nodes.label: Heats evenly without rotating food
new_nodes.detail: The stirrer takes over the turntable's uniform-heating job.

ideas.rationale: With nothing to misfit, reseat or clean around, loading is simply put the plate down and press start.

ideas.title: Solid-state GaN amplifier replaces magnetron and HV chain

new_nodes.label: GaN solid-state RF amplifier module
new_nodes.detail: Transistor amplifier on a low-voltage DC rail replaces the magnetron tube, with no cathode to wear and no 4 kV supply.

new_nodes.label: GaN HEMT RF amplification
new_nodes.detail: Wide-bandgap transistors amplify RF directly at 2.45 GHz from a 48 V rail.

new_nodes.label: Switch-mode 48 V DC supply
new_nodes.detail: Compact high-frequency converter replaces the 50 Hz iron-core HV transformer, capacitor and diode stack.

new_nodes.label: Wide-bandgap high-frequency switching
new_nodes.detail: Fast GaN or SiC switching gives efficient conversion with negligible no-load loss.

new_nodes.label: Zone-selective RF power delivery
new_nodes.detail: Per-feed amplitude and phase control sends energy into the food rather than into cavity air and walls.

new_nodes.label: Higher solid-state cost per watt
new_nodes.detail: Transistor RF modules cost more than a magnetron at 700 W and need heatsinking.

ideas.rationale: Swapping the magnetron and 4 kV chain for a low-voltage solid-state amplifier removes transformer no-load and magnetron warm-up losses and steers energy into the food, so fewer watt-hours are spent heating air and walls.

ideas.title: Phased multi-feed field sweep replaces the turntable

new_nodes.label: Four-port phased feed array
new_nodes.detail: Feed points in the cavity walls are driven from one source through RF phase shifters, with no moving parts.

new_nodes.label: Electronic RF phase steering
new_nodes.detail: Relative phase between feeds moves the interference pattern so hot and cold spots sweep without rotation.

new_nodes.label: Electronic field sweep
new_nodes.detail: Moves the standing-wave pattern across the food, replacing mechanical rotation.

new_nodes.label: Phase-shifter insertion loss
new_nodes.detail: Phase shifters and splitters add RF loss that must be kept small to protect efficiency.

ideas.title: Solid-State Thaw Engine

new_nodes.label: GaN solid-state 2.45 GHz amplifier
new_nodes.detail: Low-voltage transistor amplifier replaces the magnetron and its high-voltage transformer, capacitor and diode chain.

new_nodes.label: GaN HEMT power transistors
new_nodes.detail: Gallium nitride transistors generate 2.45 GHz RF efficiently from low-voltage DC.

new_nodes.label: Continuously variable RF power control
new_nodes.detail: Analog gain sets power in fine steps, replacing the 30 s on/off duty-cycle cam.

new_nodes.label: Gentle continuous thaw
new_nodes.detail: Steady low power lets ice melt inward without the surface edges cooking first.

ideas.rationale: Continuous, fine-grained low power lets frozen food thaw evenly, avoiding the on/off surges that cook the edges while the centre stays icy.

ideas.title: 27 MHz Capacitive Thaw Plates

new_nodes.label: Copper thaw electrode pair (27.12 MHz)
new_nodes.detail: Food sits between two plates, and the field soaks through thick frozen blocks in one pass.

new_nodes.label: Low-cost RF oscillator with matching network
new_nodes.detail: A cheap discrete oscillator and LC network replace the magnetron, waveguide and HV transformer.

new_nodes.label: Capacitive RF tempering
new_nodes.detail: Long-wavelength fields heat food throughout its volume rather than from the surface inward.

new_nodes.label: Deep uniform thaw of dense frozen blocks
new_nodes.detail: Deep penetration at 27 MHz gives even thawing with no standing-wave hot spots.

new_edges.from: Low-cost RF oscillator with matching network
Low-cost RF oscillator with matching network
Low-cost RF oscillator with matching network

new_edges.to: Deep uniform thaw of dense frozen blocks

new_edges.from: Deep uniform thaw of dense frozen blocks

ideas.rationale: Long-wavelength fields penetrate thick frozen blocks in one pass, so the centre thaws alongside the outside instead of waiting for surface heat to travel inward.

ideas.title: Curie-Point Thaw Plate

new_nodes.label: Ferrite-ceramic thaw plate
new_nodes.detail: A fixed plate absorbs stray microwaves and conducts heat into the underside of the food.

new_nodes.label: Self-limiting ferrite microwave absorption
new_nodes.detail: Magnetic loss falls sharply near the Curie point, capping plate temperature without a thermostat.

new_nodes.label: Conducts heat into the food base
new_nodes.detail: Contact conduction warms the cold underside that stalls thawing of dense blocks.

new_edges.to: Conducts heat into the food base

new_edges.from: Conducts heat into the food base

ideas.rationale: Heat entering from below removes the cold base that stalls thawing of dense blocks, and with no motor or roller ring there is nothing to wear out.

ideas.title: Thaw-Endpoint Current Sense

new_nodes.label: Shunt resistor on transformer primary
new_nodes.detail: One low-cost resistor reads load changes, so no extra sensor is needed.

new_nodes.label: Microcontroller thaw firmware
new_nodes.detail: Runs a thaw curve and stops when the current signature shows the ice has turned to water.

new_nodes.label: Load-impedance sensing via current signature
new_nodes.detail: Ice (low loss) to water (high loss) shifts absorbed power, and therefore the current draw.

new_nodes.label: Auto-detects thaw endpoint
new_nodes.detail: Ends the cycle at the right moment, so the user never has to guess time or power.

ideas.rationale: Sensing the moment ice turns to water lets the oven stop at exactly the right point, so frozen food is fully thawed without guesswork or overcooked edges.

ideas.title: Waste-Heat Steam Thaw

new_nodes.label: Copper heat pipe with water pan
new_nodes.detail: A passive heat pipe carries magnetron waste heat to a shallow water pan whose steam is vented into the cavity.

new_nodes.label: Passive heat-pipe heat transport
new_nodes.detail: Evaporation and condensation inside a sealed copper tube move heat with no moving parts.

new_nodes.label: Generates steam for latent-heat thaw
new_nodes.detail: Steam condensing on frozen surfaces releases heat quickly and evenly across the food.

new_edges.from: Copper heat pipe with water pan

ideas.rationale: Magnetron heat that is currently blown away becomes steam that condenses onto frozen food, adding fast, even latent heat to the defrost while removing the fan motor.

ideas.title: Load-sensing magnetron replaces the timer cam

new_nodes.detail: Food absorbs microwave energy, so mains current and absorbed power change along a readable curve.

new_nodes.label: Solid-state load monitor
new_nodes.detail: A current shunt and microcontroller replace the synchronous motor, cam, spring and switch.

new_nodes.label: Infers food state from absorbed-power curve

new_edges.from: Infers food state from absorbed-power curve
Infers food state from absorbed-power curve

ideas.rationale: Reading what the food is actually absorbing gives the user a readiness signal grounded in the food's state rather than elapsed time.

ideas.title: Smell-to-light doneness bar replaces the lamp

new_nodes.label: Metal-oxide VOC and humidity sensing
new_nodes.detail: Cheap solid-state sensors respond to aroma compounds and steam as food browns and dries.

new_nodes.label: Gas and humidity sensor pad
new_nodes.detail: One sensor chip in the cavity vent replaces the lamp socket and its wiring.

new_nodes.label: Detects aroma and steam from the cavity
new_nodes.detail: Measures volatile compounds and humidity rising from the food.

new_nodes.label: Doneness LED bar
new_nodes.detail: A short row of LEDs on the control panel fills as aroma and steam build up.

new_nodes.label: Shows readiness trend without looking inside
new_nodes.detail: Maps aroma and steam intensity to a visible readiness level.

new_edges.to: Detects aroma and steam from the cavity
Shows readiness trend without looking inside

new_edges.from: Detects aroma and steam from the cavity
new_edges.to: Shows readiness trend without looking inside

new_edges.from: Shows readiness trend without looking inside
Shows readiness trend without looking inside

ideas.rationale: Aroma and steam often change before the surface looks done, so a readiness bar driven by them tells the user when food is nearly ready even with the door closed.

ideas.title: Food-sound doneness chime replaces the bell

new_nodes.label: Acoustic emission sensing of food activity
new_nodes.detail: Popping, sizzling and bubbling fall away as food finishes, and a contact piezo can track that decay.

new_nodes.label: Piezo listener and chime
new_nodes.detail: One piezo element listens for food sounds, then sounds the chime, replacing the hammer and metal bell.

new_nodes.label: Signals readiness from the food's own sound
new_nodes.detail: Alerts when acoustic activity decays toward silence, not when a clock runs out.

new_edges.to: Acoustic emission sensing of food activity

new_edges.from: Acoustic emission sensing of food activity
Acoustic emission sensing of food activity

new_edges.to: Signals readiness from the food's own sound

new_edges.from: Signals readiness from the food's own sound
Signals readiness from the food's own sound

ideas.rationale: Alerting on the acoustic decay of the food itself tells the user the food is ready, not merely that a clock has run out.

ideas.title: Door pops ajar at end of cycle

new_nodes.label: Pre-loaded spring latch release
new_nodes.detail: Stored spring energy is released mechanically, the same principle as the existing push-release button.

new_nodes.label: Spring-assisted door pop-out
new_nodes.detail: After the cam cuts power, a pre-loaded spring lifts the door 1-2 cm ajar, replacing the bell hammer.

new_nodes.label: Physical end-of-cook signal
new_nodes.detail: A visible door gap and a felt movement announce the end with no sound and no electronics.

ideas.rationale: A door that physically opens a crack is an unmissable, silent cue that cooking has finished, so the user knows to check the food without needing to hear a bell or peer inside.

ideas.title: Turntable doubles as a scale tracking moisture loss

new_nodes.label: Strain-gauge turntable hub
new_nodes.detail: The turntable sits on a load cell, so mass lost to evaporation is tracked in real time.

new_nodes.label: Strain-gauge load cell
new_nodes.detail: A bonded foil strain gauge with a bridge amplifier, a cheap and proven weighing method.

new_nodes.label: Tracks food moisture loss as doneness proxy
new_nodes.detail: Calls the food ready when its mass has dropped by a food-specific fraction.

new_nodes.label: Liquid sloshing corrupts weight signal
new_nodes.detail: Moving liquids and spills add noise to the mass reading.

new_edges.to: Tracks food moisture loss as doneness proxy

new_edges.from: Tracks food moisture loss as doneness proxy
Tracks food moisture loss as doneness proxy
Tracks food moisture loss as doneness proxy

new_edges.to: Tracks food moisture loss as doneness proxy

ideas.rationale: Real-time mass loss tracks moisture leaving the food, the physical process behind doneness, so the oven can declare the food ready from the food itself rather than from a clock.

new_nodes.detail: Timer cam releases a spring latch that pushes the door ajar about 15 mm after RF is already off, replacing the bell striker.

new_nodes.label: Cam-driven spring latch release
new_nodes.detail: Reuses the existing timer cam and latch lever so the door itself becomes the alarm.

new_nodes.label: Physically presents finished state (door pops ajar)
new_nodes.detail: Tactile and visual end-of-cook cue, readable by touch, by sight across the room, or by the click of the latch.

new_edges.to: Physically presents finished state (door pops ajar)

ideas.rationale: Making the door itself the alarm gives an unmissable tactile and visual end-of-cook signal with no electronics, so users who cannot see, hear, or stand by the appliance still know the food is ready.

ideas.title: Load-Current Auto-Stop

new_nodes.label: Primary-side current-sense shunt
new_nodes.detail: Low-value shunt on the transformer primary reads magnetron load current, which shifts as food absorbs energy, replacing the blind countdown.

new_nodes.label: Load-dependent magnetron current signature
new_nodes.detail: Input current tracks cavity load mismatch and plateaus when food reaches its target dielectric state.

new_nodes.label: Detects food absorption state (closed-loop doneness)
new_nodes.detail: Ends or flags cooking when the current signature plateaus, with the timer kept only as a safety ceiling.

ideas.rationale: The microwave stops when the food itself signals readiness by reading the load current the magnetron already draws, giving the user reliable feedback without guessing at times.

ideas.title: Pinhole Thermopile Warmth Bar

new_nodes.label: Single-pixel IR thermopile behind sub-wavelength pinhole
new_nodes.detail: A roughly 1 mm pinhole in the cavity wall passes infrared but blocks 2.45 GHz, and a thermopile aimed at the food reads surface temperature for a few cents of BOM.

new_nodes.label: Sub-wavelength aperture thermal sensing
new_nodes.detail: A hole much smaller than 12.2 cm is RF-opaque but IR-transparent, extending the Faraday-cage principle to thermal vision.

new_nodes.label: Shows food temperature state as a warmth bar
new_nodes.detail: A row of LEDs on the fascia fills from cold to 74C, replacing a lamp that only shows the food is being cooked.
